topics.title: FCA SM&CR Phase 2 — Certification Regime abolition proposed
topics.summary:
FCA CP26/37 proposes abolishing the Certification Regime and FCA Directory in the most significant SM&CR reform since 2016. Pre-approval retained only for CEO, CFO, CRO, and board chair. Estimated £2 billion, 10-year compliance saving.

• Firms must review all Certified Function holders against new framework
• Conduct Rules notification replaces mandatory annual training
• FCA Directory decommissioned — firms lose public disclosure requirement
• Board attestation obligations under SYSC 4.7 unchanged
topics.insight: Firms with large Certification populations (retail banks, wealth managers) gain most. However, internal accountability frameworks must be redesigned before abolition date to avoid governance gaps.
key_actions: Map all current Certified Function holders to remaining controlled functions
Review employment contracts referencing Certification Regime obligations
Submit CP26/37 consultation response before 22 January 2027
Update CASS Oversight Function documentation under new SM&CR framework

topics.title: CASS 15 live — payment firms now under safeguarding rulebook
topics.summary:
CASS 15 (from PS25/12) entered force 7 May 2026, introducing structured safeguarding obligations for EMIs and payment service firms:

• Daily reconciliations of safeguarded funds against safeguarding ledger
• Monthly REP027 returns to FCA
• Annual safeguarding audit for firms holding over £100,000 client funds
• Resolution pack retrievable within 48 hours
• Firms must hold funds only in designated safeguarding accounts
topics.insight: Payment firms that relied on the old, less prescriptive PSRs safeguarding arrangements are now under CASS 6/7-equivalent scrutiny. CASS Oversight Function holders at dual-regulated firms must extend oversight scope to cover CASS 15 entities.
key_actions: Confirm CASS 15 reconciliation process is operational and documented
Verify REP027 monthly return has been submitted for October 2026
Review resolution pack completeness — 48-hour retrieval test required
Extend CASS oversight to cover any group EMI/payment subsidiaries

topics.title: BofA $1.21B FinCEN/OCC/OFAC AML penalty — systemic programme failures
topics.summary:
Bank of America received a combined $1.21 billion enforcement action from three US regulators for systemic AML and sanctions failures spanning 2019–2024:

• FinCEN: $500M civil money penalty for transaction monitoring failures
• OCC: $450M for correspondent banking control deficiencies
• OFAC: $260M for apparent sanctions violations in SWIFT payment processing
• BofA subject to monitorship and enhanced AML compliance programme
• Key failure: inadequate beneficial ownership screening for shell company customers
topics.insight: The largest combined US AML penalty of 2026 signals regulators will pursue systemic failures across all three major AML pillars simultaneously. Banks with large correspondent banking networks should conduct urgent gap analysis against BofA's consent order requirements.
key_actions: Review correspondent banking CDD programme against FinCEN consent order requirements
Test OFAC sanctions screening coverage for SWIFT MT103/MT202 COV messages
Conduct gap analysis on shell company beneficial ownership verification procedures
Escalate to Board Risk Committee: systemic AML monitoring coverage metrics

topics.title: SEC/CFTC joint crypto framework — DeFi protocols face first registration requirements
topics.summary:
The SEC and CFTC published a joint final rule establishing a coordinated framework for crypto asset intermediaries in the US:

• DeFi protocols >$100M TVL must register as swap execution facilities (CFTC) or alternative trading systems (SEC)
• New crypto broker-dealer lite regime for intermediaries under $500M AUM
• Mandatory custody and segregation requirements for all registered VASPs
• Stablecoin issuers must hold 1:1 reserve assets in US-regulated banks
• First mandatory registration regime directly targeting DeFi protocols and startups
topics.insight: The joint framework ends regulatory arbitrage between SEC and CFTC crypto jurisdiction. DeFi protocols must structurally decide whether to register, restrict US user access, or challenge the rules in court. Many VC-backed crypto startups will need compliance counsel urgently.
key_actions: Assess whether any crypto platform holdings cross $100M TVL threshold
Review DeFi protocol exposure in investment portfolios for regulatory risk
Monitor litigation timeline — industry challenge expected Q1 2027
Update crypto AML policies to reference new registered VASP requirements

topics.title: MAS revokes Sir Money Changer licence — AML/CFT failures across all control layers
topics.summary:
MAS revoked the Major Payment Institution licence of Sir Money Changer Pte Ltd on 14 October 2026 for repeated AML/CFT failures:

• Failed to perform CDD for cash transactions above S$5,000 threshold (3 years)
• Did not retain transaction records as required under MAS Notice PSN01
• Failed to file suspicious transaction reports for high-risk customers
• Licence revocation is MAS's most severe sanction short of criminal prosecution
• Customers must complete all pending transactions before 14 November 2026
topics.insight: MAS's willingness to revoke a Major Payment Institution licence for cumulative CDD failures (rather than a single egregious breach) signals a zero-tolerance posture for AML control gaps across Singapore's payment sector. PSPs and money changers should conduct immediate CDD process audits.
key_actions: Review CDD procedures for cash transactions at all threshold levels (S$5,000+, S$20,000+)
Verify suspicious transaction report (STR) filing completeness for past 36 months
Conduct MAS Notice PSN01 recordkeeping audit — 5-year retention requirement
Brief Board Risk Committee on MAS enforcement posture change

topics.title: ASIC A$4.356M infringement notices — 22 companies including 5 fintech operators
topics.summary:
ASIC issued A$4.356 million in infringement notices against 22 companies for AFSL and ACL breaches:

• 5 of the 22 companies are fintech operators offering embedded lending products
• Breaches: operating without licence, failing to meet licence conditions, inadequate hardship processes
• ASIC notes embedded lending in non-financial platforms as growing regulatory risk
• Infringement notices do not require admission of liability
• Highest single notice: A$395,000 against a BNPL provider for failure to assess suitability
topics.insight: ASIC's targeting of embedded fintech lending (BNPL-style products in retail, telco and utilities platforms) confirms the regulator is extending its surveillance beyond traditional finance into platform economy credit. Firms with API-distributed lending products must review their AFSL coverage.
key_actions: Audit all embedded lending products for AFSL/ACL coverage
Review suitability assessment procedures for BNPL and similar products
Check hardship policy compliance under RG 271
Register all API-distributed credit products with ASIC credit register

topics.title: FSCA record R2.8bn penalties — Banxso deepfake AI fraud signals new threat class
topics.summary:
The FSCA's 2025/2026 Regulatory Actions Report reveals a 23-fold increase in penalties, dominated by the Banxso deepfake fraud:

• AI-generated deepfakes of Elon Musk and Johann Rupert used to market unlawful investment scheme
• Approximately R1 billion in client funds misappropriated
• Directors Harel Sekler and Warwick Sneider fined over R2 billion combined
• Debarment for up to 30 years; matter referred to South African Police
• Firm liquidated — FSCA seeking restitution for affected investors
topics.insight: Deepfake-enabled investment fraud now represents a primary threat vector in African retail financial markets. Financial institutions must implement synthetic media detection controls in their marketing compliance and consumer-facing communications review processes.
key_actions: Implement deepfake/synthetic media detection in KYC video verification procedures
Brief marketing compliance team on FSCA deepfake enforcement precedent
Review social media monitoring programme for impersonation of firm executives
Update investor communications policy to address AI-generated fraud disclosures

topics.title: CBN data localisation mandate — payment firms must store data in Nigeria by 31 Dec 2026
topics.summary:
CBN Circular PSS/DIR/PUB/CIR/001/004 imposes four simultaneous interventions:

• Mandatory payment transaction data storage within Nigeria — 31 December 2026 deadline
• Market share concentration caps for dominant payment processors
• Mandatory Ultimate Beneficial Ownership disclosure for all payment businesses
• Enhanced systemic oversight measures effective 1 January 2027
• Non-compliant firms face licence suspension after 1 January 2027
• Fintechs with AWS/Google Cloud cross-border data arrangements face significant operational restructuring
topics.insight: The 31 December 2026 data localisation deadline is six weeks away. Fintechs relying on hyperscaler infrastructure outside Nigeria must urgently assess whether local data centres can be provisioned in time or whether temporary licence suspension risk is acceptable.
key_actions: Assess current payment transaction data storage locations against Nigeria localisation requirement
Engage AWS/Google/Azure for Nigeria-region data storage options
File UBO disclosure documentation with CBN before December 2026
Review market share calculations against CBN concentration cap thresholds

topics.title: BCB VASP enforcement — banks prohibited from dealings with unlicensed crypto operators
topics.summary:
BCB's Virtual Assets Law enforcement phase activated 30 October 2026:

• All BCB-supervised banks prohibited from maintaining relationships with unlicensed VASPs
• Institutions still dealing with unauthorised VASPs must cease within 30 days
• BCB Resolutions 519–521 require VASPs to hold BCB authorisation to operate
• Over 40 crypto startups had not yet filed for BCB authorisation at the deadline
• Stablecoin issuers and DeFi protocols explicitly in scope of the VASP definition
topics.insight: Brazil's VASP enforcement creates immediate compliance risk for banks and payment institutions with crypto B2B relationships. Firms must audit all crypto-sector counterparties and obtain BCB authorisation confirmation or terminate relationships within 30 days.
key_actions: Audit all crypto-sector counterparty relationships for BCB VASP authorisation status
Issue 30-day notice to terminate relationships with unauthorised VASPs
Update AML/KYB (Know Your Business) programme to include BCB VASP registry check
Review correspondent banking agreements for crypto exposure

topics.title: FATF Grey List update: Bolivia, Haiti, Venezuela retained — correspondent banking impact
topics.summary:
FATF October 2026 Plenary outcomes for Latin America:

• Bolivia, Haiti, Venezuela remain under increased monitoring
• Key deficiencies: weak VASP supervision, beneficial ownership transparency gaps, low asset recovery rates
• Four jurisdictions globally exited the grey list (not LatAm)
• GAFILAT typologies report highlighted trade-based money laundering and crypto exposure
• De-risking pressure from correspondent banks expected to intensify for grey-listed jurisdictions
topics.insight: Financial institutions processing payments to or from Bolivia, Haiti, and Venezuela must maintain enhanced due diligence programmes that document FATF grey list status. Correspondent banking agreements with banks in those countries should be reviewed annually.
key_actions: Update EDD programme for all transactions involving Bolivia, Haiti, Venezuela
Review correspondent bank agreements for grey-listed jurisdiction counterparties
Brief MLCO on GAFILAT typologies report — trade-based ML and crypto vectors
Update FATF grey list status in AML risk rating matrix

topics.title: DORA enforcement commences 17 January 2027 — EBA finds 61% of firms non-compliant
topics.summary:
EBA's October 2026 DORA readiness review:

• 61% of EU financial institutions not fully compliant with DORA requirements
• Largest gaps: ICT third-party risk management (74% non-compliant) and digital operational resilience testing (68% non-compliant)
• Major ICT-related incidents reported to NCAs up 34% year-on-year in 2026
• DORA formal enforcement with sanctioning powers begins 17 January 2027
• Early enforcement focus: ICT incident classification accuracy and TLPT/TIBER-EU test results
topics.insight: With 10 weeks to the enforcement start date and 61% of institutions still non-compliant, the EBA gap suggests NCAs will initially focus enforcement on the most systemic institutions. Firms should prioritise ICT third-party risk registers and incident classification policies as minimum viable compliance.
key_actions: Complete DORA ICT third-party risk register — all critical ICT vendors documented
Classify all ICT vendors by DORA criticality tier before 17 January 2027
Ensure ICT incident classification framework aligns with EBA RTS on major incidents
Submit TLPT/TIBER-EU test timeline to competent authority if not yet completed

topics.title: MiCA CASP enforcement phase — ESMA targets 23 non-compliant jurisdictions
topics.summary:
ESMA's MiCA supervisory enforcement phase update:

• 23 EU member states still have CASPs operating under expired transitional arrangements
• ESMA has established supervisory colleges for major CASPs above €1 billion AUM (Q1 2027)
• MiCA authorisation requirement for crypto startups — full CASP licence mandatory
• Trading platforms, custody providers, and stablecoin issuers all in scope
• NCAs must report all operating-without-authorisation cases to ESMA by 31 December 2026
topics.insight: Crypto startups operating in EU markets under informal or transitional arrangements face imminent enforcement. Firms that have not yet filed MiCA CASP applications should do so immediately — processing times are running 4–6 months at most NCAs.
key_actions: Confirm MiCA CASP application has been submitted to relevant NCA
Review crypto service scope against MiCA Annex I permitted activities
Ensure AML/CFT policies reference MiCA Travel Rule requirements
Brief legal counsel on ESMA college supervisory scope if >€1B AUM
